note: Shows a step-choice as variants: each chip sets a key and a position together, so two scales that sit in the same part of the neck can be compared on one neck. The why says what links them (four shared notes), and the text says what to look for between the two (one note moves, the ringed roots change places) instead of asking the learner to find it.

exercise.title: One place on the neck, two keys
exercise.focus: A minor pentatonic position 1 and E minor pentatonic position 3 · the same frets · over a drone
exercise.why: A minor and E minor pentatonic share four of their five notes, so in the same part of the neck only one note moves and the root is a new note to end on.

sections.text:
Press Play below to start the drone. Play the position on the neck up and back down, and end on a ringed {{1}}.
Then try the other variant. Use the Variant selector below to change it, then press Play to start the drone again, now on the new root.
When you change the variant, your hand stays in the same part of the neck: one note sits a fret lower, and the ringed notes are in new places. Go back and forth between the two until you can end a phrase on a ringed {{1}} in either.
